title: Information Channels
description: How much can be said across a distance, through noise? Friis: a signal spreads out, so the power caught falls as the square of the distance, and a bigger dish catches more. Johnson and Nyquist: every receiver hisses with noise proportional to its temperature and its bandwidth, which is why the deep space dishes cool theirs. Shannon: the rate a channel can carry without error is its bandwidth times the logarithm of one plus the signal over the noise. Voyager, beyond the planets, still sends 160 bits a second. Unlocks the Deep Space Transceiver.

puzzle.goal: A channel of bandwidth B carries a signal of power S over noise N. Write the most bits a second it can carry without error, C (Shannon and Hartley).
puzzle.name: Channel capacity
puzzle.ask: Find C in bit/s for a 4000 Hz line with S/N = @{S}.
puzzle.method: Count how many signal levels the noise lets you tell apart, √(1 + S/N), sending 2B symbols a second.
